text:
maya: Heads up — after the driver hotpatch to nv-driver 534.23 we started seeing MIG profile assignments go missing / remapped in us-west1-c. Pods that bind to specific sub-devices are failing with NCCL errors.

dylan: Which nodes are affected? any pattern (kernel, instance type)?

maya: node-ish-uwc-12, node-ish-uwc-14, node-ish-uwc-20. All GFNX A100s, kernel 6.1.0-25. Looks like the NVML UUIDs shifted and the old mapping in our device-plugin no longer matches.

aditya: Can you paste nvidia-smi from one of the nodes?

maya: Sure — here's the relevant bits from node-ish-uwc-12: 
```
$ nvidia-smi -q -i 0 | egrep "UUID|MIG"
GPU UUID                              : GPU-1a2b3c4d-OLD
MIG Mode                               : Enabled
MIG Devices                            : No MIG devices found

# after driver reload
GPU UUID                              : GPU-5f6e7d8c-NEW
MIG Mode                               : Enabled
MIG Devices                            : 7 active instances
```
The device-plugin had cached the old GPU UUID -> pod assignment, so pods are binding to nonexistent UUIDs.

gwen: infra-bot shows the node-level driver rollout completed at 1934567600. No reboots were performed (hotpatch). Maybe NVML behavior changed between 534.16 and 534.23 where the ordering/UUID exposure is non-deterministic until the kernel module is fully reloaded.

infra-bot: driver-rollout/us-west1-c completed for group gpu-pool-uwc at 1934567600. No reboots executed.

dylan: Two things: (1) we should avoid in-place driver swaps without pod drains on MIG machines; (2) quick mitigation: taint affected nodes and move pods to healthy hosts.

aditya: Agreed. Also we can run a small script to regenerate the mapping from current NVML output and update the device-plugin registry. Minimal steps: 
```bash
# on node
sudo systemctl stop kubelet
sudo modprobe -r nvidia_uvm nvidia_drm nvidia
sudo modprobe nvidia
sudo systemctl start kubelet
# then recreate MIG profiles if missing
sudo nvidia-smi mig -C  # clear any broken profiles
sudo nvidia-smi mig -cgi 19,19,19 -i 0  # example create profiles
```
But clearing profiles is intrusive.

maya: We tried a soft restart of gpu-manager and device-plugin; after that one node showed MIG again but with new UUIDs and pods still failed. Recreating profiles on the node restored workloads but assigned different sub-device IDs than the scheduler expected.

sre-oncall: This is touching running customer infra — start an incident? we should notify cs.

maya: Opened INC-2026. Temporary mitigation: cordon/taint and move non-critical jobs, manual recreate for critical ones.

gwen: Also saw NVML logs: /var/log/nvidia/gpu-manager.log contains repeated lines: 
```
NVML: Warning: GPU UUID mismatch detected: mapped GPU-1a2b3c4d-OLD -> GPU-5f6e7d8c-NEW
NVML: Error: MIG device index not found for UUID GPU-1a2b3c4d-OLD
```

aditya: Two potential longer-term fixes: pin driver version for GPU pools until we validate, or update device-plugin to match GPUs by PCI bus ID / physical index in addition to UUID (more robust).

dylan: For immediate next steps: 
- mark affected nodes unschedulable (maya)
- run our mapping script to emit PCI->UUID->MIG mapping (aditya)
- if necessary, recreate profiles only on critical nodes (gwen)
- postmortem + rollback decision by EOD (dylan)

maya: I'm running the mapping script now — output snippet: 
```
GPUIndex,PCI,BDF,UUID,MIGCount
0,0000:65:00.0,65:00.0,GPU-5f6e7d8c-NEW,7
1,0000:66:00.0,66:00.0,GPU-aa11bb22-NEW,0
```

gwen: Thanks — that helps. If device-plugin used PCI BDF we could rebind pods correctly.

aditya: As a short-term automation I'll push a small device-plugin patch that prefers PCI bus mapping when UUID binding fails; will roll to a single node group for testing.

maya: FYI customer impact: 12 pods in prod degraded, all in us-west1-c. Cost note: if we recreate profiles we might temporarily lose running batch work — communicating to barbara in CS.

dylan: Good catch. Let's avoid full fleet-wide clear unless we plan a maintenance window and reboots.

infra-bot: action required: tag nodes node-ish-uwc-12, node-ish-uwc-14, node-ish-uwc-20 as affected.

maya: Action items captured in INC-2026. I'll start cordoning the nodes and schedule a controlled rollback to 534.16 on one host for validation.

aditya: Patch PR: github.com/redwood-inference/device-plugin/pull/482 (tests + fallback to PCI mapping).

dylan: Great. Keep updates in INC-2026 and thread here. :thumbsup:

gwen: One more note — check kernel module versions on rebooted nodes; we saw one node where /lib/modules had both 525 and 534 kernels present causing DKMS shims to pick the wrong module on hot-reload.

maya: Copy. Will verify module lists and follow up.

sre-oncall: If replication occurs in other regions we'll escalate. For now, us-west1-c containment looks ok.

maya: Update: recreated MIG profiles on 2 critical nodes, pods recovered. Will keep the remaining 1 cordoned until patch lands.

aditya: I'll push the device-plugin patch to canary by 1934568200.

maya: Thanks all — closing the thread here, continuing in INC-2026 for the postmortem and rollback discussion.
